newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, international accounting rules compatible.
newsitem.headline: EU, international accounting rules compatible.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday that EU and international accounting standards were compatible, clearing the way for companies seeking foreign stock exchange listings to adopt a single set of rules.

"EU rules on consolidated accounts of groups of companies, as established in (EU) accounting directives, are compatible with International Accounting Standards (IAS) set by the International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC)", the Commission said in a statement.
Currently EU-based companies that want to be quoted on an exchange outside the 15-nation bloc must prepare two or more sets of accounts which is both expensive and confusing.

There are about 80 European companies listed on the NASDAQ -- National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotation -- exchange of the United States. Its recent European offspring EASDAQ also requires potential candidates to report in international accounting standards.

"Preparing more than one set of consolidated accounts not only imposes a costly administrative burden on such companies but can also give rise to confusion amongst users of accounts, especially shareholders," the Commission said.
It was reporting on a study which compares the bloc's accounting directives with the international norms issued by the end of 1995.
The work focused on consolidated accounts of groups of companies because these are the accounts requested by capital markets worldwide.

The study, "An examination of the conformity between international accounting standards and the European accounting directives", is available from the EU's Office of Publications in Luxembourg. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
